actions.reason: BasicTokenizer.train built the initial pair counts by concatenating every adjacent pair of characters into a new 2-char str and hashing it, one per input byte. The raw bytes are now read through memoryview.cast("H") at even and odd offsets, so each pair is counted in C as a 16-bit int (byte order checked once at import). Only the distinct pairs are converted to the same 2-char str keys afterwards. Counts are identical; heap order does not depend on dict insertion order, so merges are unchanged. The initial vocab is also copied from BYTE_VOCAB instead of being rebuilt with a comprehension. Measured train_basic_ir ratio 0.9568, outputs identical.

diff --git a/minbpe/basic.py b/minbpe/basic.py
--- a/minbpe/basic.py
+++ b/minbpe/basic.py
@@ -17,7 +17,7 @@ except ImportError:
     from heapq import heapify, heappop, heappush, heapreplace
 from operator import itemgetter
 
-from .base import Tokenizer, get_stats, merge, build_merge_map, ordered_merge_steps
+from .base import Tokenizer, get_stats, merge, build_merge_map, ordered_merge_steps, BYTE_VOCAB
 
 try:
     # the C counting loop behind collections.Counter; importing it directly
@@ -30,6 +30,9 @@ except ImportError:
             mapping[elem] = get(elem, 0) + 1
 
 
+_BIG_ENDIAN = memoryview(b"\x00\x01").cast("H")[0] == 1
+
+
 def _count(iterable):
     # plain-dict equivalent of collections.Counter(iterable): same counts,
     # same insertion order
@@ -55,10 +58,17 @@ class BasicTokenizer(Tokenizer):
 
         # iteratively merge the most common pairs to create new tokens
         merges = {} # (int, int) -> int
-        vocab = {idx: bytes([idx]) for idx in range(256)} # int -> bytes
+        vocab = dict(BYTE_VOCAB) # int -> bytes
         # count up the number of times every consecutive pair appears, keyed by
         # the two-character string; kept up to date incrementally after each merge
-        stats = _count(map(str.__add__, ids, ids[1:]))
+        # (the bytes are first read as 16-bit words at even and odd offsets, so
+        # each pair is counted as a small int and only distinct pairs become str)
+        words = {}
+        for k in (0, 1):
+            w = text_bytes[k:]
+            _count_elements(words, memoryview(w[:len(w) & ~1]).cast("H"))
+        lo, hi = (8, 0) if _BIG_ENDIAN else (0, 8)
+        stats = {chr(w >> lo & 255) + chr(w >> hi & 255): n for w, n in words.items()}
         # lazy max-heap of (-count, pair); entries whose count no longer
         # matches stats are stale and dropped when they reach the top
         heap = [(-n, p) for p, n in stats.items()]

journal.text:
I changed BasicTokenizer.train in minbpe/basic.py. It built the initial pair counts by concatenating each adjacent character pair into a new 2-char str and hashing it, one per input byte. Now the raw bytes are read through memoryview.cast("H") at even and odd offsets, so each pair is counted in C as a 16-bit int. Byte order is checked once at import. Only the distinct pairs are converted back to the same 2-char str keys afterward. There were four edits, 16 changed lines.

In my sandbox, train_basic_ir went from 277759137 to 265761025, ratio 0.9568. Outputs were identical. The other metrics barely moved: train_regex_ir 1.0014, encode_ir 1.0021, decode_ir 0.9986, save_load_ir 1.0010. The guard was ok. I submitted it, and it is waiting on replays.

The initial count was per-byte Python work. The merge loop after it is untouched and probably holds most of the remaining cost.

Next I will read the merge loop in basic.py and measure how much each merge step costs on its own.
